entries.topic: Cyrus I. Scofield's documented life to 1909: Confederate service, Kansas, US attorney, forgery case, family, conversion, ordination, Dallas

claims.text: Scofield was born 19 August 1843 in Lenawee County, Michigan; in 1861, aged 17 and visiting relatives in Lebanon, Tennessee, he enlisted as a private in the 7th Tennessee Infantry (Company H formed 28 May 1861).

He was admitted to Chimborazo Hospital No. 3, Richmond, 8 April 1862 for exposure; petitioned Secretary of War Randolph for release as a Michigan native who had enlisted underage; discharge instructions of 23 Sep 1862 cited him as 'an alien friend'; discharged 26 Sep 1862 (his own parole letter says 29 Sep). Only 373 alienage exemptions were granted in the war.

Ordered to a camp of instruction at McMinnville after discharge, he walked about 75 miles to Bowling Green, Kentucky, took the Union oath of allegiance and was paroled by Col. F. A. Dick on 18 Nov 1862; Rushing treats this as desertion.
The UDC Dallas Chapter 6 awarded him the Southern Cross of Honor in 1903 (Rushing p. 105).

Trumbull (1920) states he served through the war, was under fire in eighteen battles and that the Cross of Honor was 'awarded to him for bravery at Antietam'; Rushing finds Confederate records show nothing unusual at Antietam.
Married Leontine LeBeau Cerre in a civil ceremony in St. Louis, 27 Sep 1866; daughters Abigail and Marie Helene; son Guy Sylvester died December 1874.
Elected Republican to the Kansas House November 1871 for Atchison County, chaired the Judiciary Committee; then a seat for Nemaha County; helped elect John J. Ingalls senator in 1873.

Grant appointed him US Attorney for Kansas 19 March 1873; oath 8 June 1873; resigned 20 December 1873; on 15 Dec he declined to prosecute Senator Pomeroy, the day the Chicago Tribune reported affidavits.
The DOJ's Kansas US Attorney history says he 'was forced to resign from that position due to questionable financial transactions' and shortly after was 'jailed in St. Louis on forgery charges'.

Kansas City Journal, 28 Dec 1899, 'A Preacher with a Past', attributed the resignation to 'shady financial transactions' leaving him indebted to Atchison Republicans, including money solicited for Ingalls and kept ($2,000 from one resident). Allegations of railroad bribes and forged signatures are reported by Lutzweiler and Phillips; there was no prosecution over the Kansas period.
Trumbull says he served two years and left because politics interfered with his law work; the record shows about six months in office.

Forgery: June 1877 Jeptha Simpson alleged a note forged in sister Emeline's name; Simpson sued Aug 1877; Milwaukee arrests Nov-Dec 1877 as 'Charles Ingerson' over hotel bills; second St. Louis forgery case April 1878, continued 20 May 1878; arrested at Horicon, Wisconsin, Oct 1878 (Milwaukee Daily Sentinel 3 Oct 1878); in St. Louis jail from 8 Oct 1878 and 'remained jailed much of the year'.

On 6 Nov 1879 the court entered a nolle prosequi because the prosecution 'failed to produce enough evidence' (St. Louis Republican, Nov 1879); the Topeka Daily Capital reported his 'wealthy sister came forward' and paid off the forgeries. No conviction, no prison sentence.
He abandoned his wife and daughters; Leontine returned to Atchison and worked to support them; she divorced him on grounds of desertion in 1883.

He converted in St. Louis in 1879 (DTS; Trumbull names Thomas S. McPheeters, a lawyer); by autumn 1879 he helped Moody's St. Louis campaign and was YMCA secretary; mentored by James H. Brookes; licensed to preach 1880.
Trumbull reports he had become a heavy drinker and that after conversion 'Christ came in, and drink went out'.

Ordained a Congregationalist minister in October 1883 while the divorce was pending (Lutzweiler p. 101); pastor of First Congregational Church, Dallas (from 1882 per Trumbull; 1883 per DTS), which grew from about 14 to over 500 members by 1895; went to East Northfield 1895; returned to Dallas 1902/03-1907/09.

Remarried Hettie Hall von Wartz (1883 per Wikipedia/Lutzweiler; 1884 per Trumbull); son Noel Paul (1888-1962). Trumbull's 1920 biography does not mention his first marriage; his will omitted his daughters.
No formal academic education (Trumbull); styled himself 'Rev. C. I. Scofield, D.D.' from the early 1890s with no record of any institution granting the degree (Mangum & Sweetnam p. 46).
Died 24 July 1921 in New York.

entries.topic: Rumours about Scofield tested: prison, Canada, divorces, war record, D.D., Lotos Club and Untermyer

claims.text: Scofield-Files: held in Milwaukee then St. Louis city jails over two forged signatures on two notes; 'both charges were eventually dropped'; he never went to prison; Canadian authorities have 'no record' of the Canadian prison term Canfield floated; the site says he 'likely was guilty'.

Lotos Club membership book: Scofield's entry dated 3 March 1900, proposed by Horatio Fraser, seconded by John Elderkin; Untermyer a member since 1894; under the 1900 constitution a candidate was elected unless two negative ballots were cast; 'no evidence that they ever did meet' (archivist Nancy Johnson cited, 28 May 2026).

Canfield (1988) pp. 173-74 asked 'Why would a godly man join such a godless club?', wrote 'we assume' and 'There must have been anticipation', then named Untermyer (as quoted by Scofield-Files; not checked against the book).

Untermyer (1858-1940), corporate lawyer, counsel to the Pujo money-trust inquiry, later president of Keren Hayesod (from 1921 per Scofield-Files), co-founder of the Non-Sectarian Anti-Nazi League (1933); his Wikipedia biography does not mention Scofield.

Chain: CTRL list 16 Jul 1999 -> SweetLiberty 2001 -> Carlson 2002 -> Piper, High Priests of War (2004), first Rothschild-funding claim, no documentation -> Lutz 2005 -> Singer, whale.to 2009 -> Weir 2014 ('speculative').
Check Your Fact (12 Mar 2025) rated the Rothschild-funding claim false: 'The Scofield Bible was funded by non-Jews, according to academic research', citing Rushing on Ball and Pirie.

Mike Rothschild: 'I can't find any primary source that connects the Scofield Bible, Scofield himself, or Darby to the family'; sourcing 'impossibly thin, mostly consisting of blogs and a few podcasts'; OUP is owned by the University of Oxford.
Goeman: Fitch, Pirie and Ball were 'associated with the Plymouth Brethren'; Rothschild-claim evidence traces to dubious sources such as LaRouche publications.

entries.topic: Audit re-checks for Part Four (21 October 2026)

claims.text: Audit: Rushing dates the first Confederate Conscription Act to 9 April 1862, the day after Scofield's hospital admission; Ingalls nominated Scofield a week after taking his Senate seat; Emeline denied involvement in the Simpson note and Scofield avoided service; alias 'Cyrus Ingerson' at Horicon; after the charges were settled in November 1879 he visited a Washington Avenue mission.

Audit: the statement that Scofield 'almost certainly provided deliberately inaccurate personal information' to Who's Who and Trumbull is Wikipedia's own (fn 13, citing John D. Hannah on his secrecy), not Lutzweiler's; Wikipedia still says there is 'no extant evidence in the public records' of a jailing.
Audit: Leontine was librarian of the Atchison public library for many years; Scofield's will made no mention of his daughters and his estate, including Oxford royalties, went to Hettie and Noel.

Audit: Mike Rothschild calls Executive Intelligence Review output 'antisemitic nonsense' and says the Rothschild framing fuels antisemitic conspiracy theories; Goeman describes LaRouche as promoting conspiracy theories 'with antisemitic undertones'.
